title: Can alignment depth be increased post-hoc by fine-tuning on safety-recovery examples, without touching the base training?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling chain: a post-hoc lightweight patch for alignment depth would be immediately actionable for organizations that cannot retrain from scratch. Addresses a problem recognized as critical (shallow alignment vulnerability) with intermediate deliverables (the recovery examples dataset itself) having independent safety value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing synthetic safety-recovery examples and fine-tuning a small model is a documented workflow. Measuring KL curves before and after uses the established methodology. A beginner with mentor guidance can execute this, though data construction requires careful prompt engineering.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: construct recovery examples, fine-tune one model, measure before/after depth and ASR. Clear metrics and well-bounded experiment. Comparison to full deep alignment procedure is a nice-to-have but not required for the core result.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is largely addressed by existing work. Qi et al. (ICLR 2025) already proposed and demonstrated data augmentation with safety-recovery examples that 'deepens' safety alignment beyond initial tokens. Their augmented fine-tuning pushes KL divergence on later tokens of harmful responses to much higher levels. Multiple post-hoc safety recovery methods exist: SafeLoRA projects LoRA updates onto safety subspaces, RESTA negatively merges harmful task vectors, SafeMERGE uses selective layer-wise merging, and a dedicated ACL 2025 paper 'A Post-Hoc Approach to Safety Re-Alignment for Fine-Tuned LLMs' directly addresses this. The proposed experiment is essentially a replication of Qi et al.'s augmentation approach.

evidence: Qi et al. (2024). Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep. ICLR 2025.
A Post-Hoc Approach to Safety Re-Alignment for Fine-Tuned LLMs. ACL 2025 Findings.
SafeMERGE: Preserving Safety Alignment via Selective Layer-Wise Model Merging. arXiv:2503.17239.
SaLoRA: Safety-Alignment Preserved Low-Rank Adaptation. ICLR 2025.
